Apple has reached a $250 million class action settlement over the delayed rollout of Siri and Apple Intelligence features, and the case is now moving through the court process. Here is a breakdown of how the $250 million will be distributed, who is eligible, and other details.

Apple Siri $250 Million Settlement

Apple faced a class action lawsuit last year over multiple delays to some Siri and Apple Intelligence features, which were first unveiled at WWDC 2024. The lawsuit accused Apple of marketing and promoting AI features that either did not exist or would not be available for years.

The lawsuit claimed Apple generated an "unprecedented level of hype" around Apple Intelligence in an effort to "convince consumers to upgrade their devices at premium prices."

Apple agreed to the settlement in December, with the terms made public in May. Apple did not admit any wrongdoing in the settlement. At the time, Apple told 9to5Mac that the settlement was made to "continue focusing on what we do best — delivering innovative products and services for our users."

Apple also promoted the Apple Intelligence features that have already launched, including Writing Tools, the Clean Up feature, and Visual Intelligence.

According to MacRumors, Apple’s settlement received preliminary approval from a judge following a hearing last week on July 8, allowing the case to proceed to the next stage. The judge rejected the argument that the settlement lumped together class members with vastly different claim amounts.

Who Is Eligible

For iPhone users, the most important news is that Apple will be distributing a portion of the $250 million to affected iPhone owners.

The eligible class includes consumers who purchased iPhone models with Apple Intelligence capabilities between June 10, 2024 (when Apple announced the relevant features) and March 29, 2025 (shortly after Apple announced the delays).

The relevant device models are as follows:

  • iPhone 15 Pro
  • iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 16
  • iPhone 16 Plus
  • iPhone 16 Pro
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max

How Much Will Apple Pay iPhone Users?

The total settlement amount is $250 million, but a large portion will first go toward attorney fees and other legal expenses. For iPhone users, the estimated payout is around $25 per eligible device.

However, this amount is not fixed and will ultimately depend on the total number of claims submitted. If more eligible users file claims, the per-person payout may decrease; if fewer claims are filed, eligible device owners could receive up to $95 per device.

How to File a Claim

At this stage, eligible iPhone users do not need to take any action. The case has received preliminary approval and can proceed. According to the schedule, the notice inviting claims will be sent out within 45 days of last week’s approval, which is no later than August 31, 2026.

When submitting a claim, you will need to provide proof of purchase for the eligible device, such as a serial number. You will also need to provide your Apple account information and phone number.

The settlement administrator Verita Global will set up a website for users to submit claim information, but the site is not yet live. We will be sure to let everyone know once the site goes live.

However, it will still take some time before the payments are distributed. The final approval hearing for the payout (not just approval of the settlement terms) is not scheduled until September 29, 2027, and checks will be mailed out no sooner than 60 days after that.

Wrap-Up

Are you eligible to receive a share of Apple’s $250 million settlement over the Siri and Apple Intelligence delays? Do you think this settlement is fair? Let us know in the comments.
